newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares set high, seen losing steam.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares set high, seen losing steam.

text.p: Polish shares on Tuesday set their fifth-straight 33-month high but analysts said the market might finally be losing steam after surging 8.1 percent since last Tuesday on apparent institutional blue-chip buying.

"You can see the whole time there's foreign and institutional demand due to the kind of stocks that are going up, such as (software firm) ComputerLand and (industrial and trading firm") Elektrim," said Jan Koch of Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage.
The two stocks on Tuesday rose 9.9 percent and 7.1 percent respectively. But analysts said the market's significant post-price-fixing selling signalled a profit-taking correction.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose one percent to 15,588.8 and turnover fell 11 percent to 127.3 million zlotys ($43.9 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 34 to 33 with 17 stocks flat.

Some analysts said that demand from institutional investors, apparently acting on their picks for 1997, could prove strong enough to delay the expected correction, and that speculative post-price-fixing trade could prove misleading.
Analysts said investors would be watching Wednesday's December inflation figure to help determine if the central bank would raise interest rates, as it has warned it might to curb fast credit action.

Analysts said loss leader furniture maker Swarzedz fell 4.4 percent in profit-taking after recent gains, perhaps also hurt by Monday's news it wanted to issue more shares. The firm has said that it might issue shares for its creditors.
NFI units rose 3.2 percent to 161 zlotys ($55.5) in heavy 62-million-zloty ($21.4 million)trade.
